summary:
MARSCOPE – An Interactive Martian Exploration and Mission Planning Platform

MARSCOPE is an interactive web-based platform developed to support the planning and visualization of exploration missions on Mars. Designed in response to the NASA Space Apps Challenge theme, “Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map,” it provides users with an illustrative Martian map where they can add, edit, and manage exploration waypoints, visualize routes between locations, and calculate approximate surface distances using the Haversine formula.

The platform also allows users to export mission plans as JSON files, save waypoint data locally in their browser, and explore Mars-related imagery through NASA’s Image and Video Library.

MARSCOPE addresses the challenge by making Martian exploration planning more accessible, interactive, and understandable. It demonstrates how digital mapping and mission-planning concepts can help users organize exploration routes and visualize potential journeys across the Martian surface. Our goal is to create an educational foundation that can evolve into a more advanced mission-planning tool incorporating real scientific terrain data, environmental hazards, and rover constraints.
